summary.intent: Plan and execute GSD roadmap phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain, resolved folder listings) for cipher-box end-to-end — research, scope decisions, pattern mapping, plan generation, verification, and wave-by-wave execution — while also spinning up an independent worktree to start phase 69 in parallel.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed (12 plans/7 waves, plan-checker PASSED, coverage gates 13/13) and execution progressed through Waves 1–3 plus 4 of 5 plans in Wave 4 (8/12 plans done, all independently spot-checked and green); a clean phase-69 worktree was created off origin/main; one non-blocking coverage gap (D-03 poll-invalidation) was logged as a todo, and a planner coverage gap (unowned components consuming SealedChildRef/ResolvedChild) was surfaced for Plan 11 to absorb.

repo: gsd `worktree.baseRef` config (`head` vs `fresh`) determines whether execute-phase worktree executors fork from live HEAD or origin/main — must verify before dispatching into worktrees, since a `fresh` default would miss uncommitted PLAN.md files on the phase branch.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel execution requires a separate `pnpm install` per worktree (expensive); for phases with mostly single-plan waves, sequential execution on the main tree is more robust and reuses installed node_modules.

REQUIREMENTS.md checkbox tracking is fragile across multi-plan requirements: plan executors sometimes mark a requirement `[x]` complete when only their own task is done, even though the requirement's full acceptance criteria (e.g. deleting legacy services) span multiple later plans — needs manual verification and correction after each plan.
SDK-touching plans require rebuilding the SDK dist before running web typecheck in the same wave, otherwise web sees stale exports (cross-package staleness landmine).
The `gap-analysis.plan-post` check's generic output parser chokes on control characters in the `rendered` field — must invoke the check directly rather than through the generic parser wrapper.
gsd-tools commit helper's `commit_failed` report is a known false negative — always confirm via `git log` before treating it as a real failure (reconfirms existing memory).

code.finding: Plan 68.2-01 added the ROT-07 anti-rollback gate (`RotationHighWater.enforceResolved`) to `resolvePublishedNode` (root resolve) as one of two new read-path gating sites, alongside the pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156.
Second new gating site added by plan 68.2-01: `dfsFindFolder`'s child loop now enforces the same ROT-07 read-path gate.

`resolveChildren`'s per-child skip-on-resolve/unseal-failure degradation is security-sound: the target folder is already gated via Plan-01's `ensureFolderLoaded`/`dfsFindFolder` before this runs, so an unverifiable sibling is simply omitted from the listing rather than rendered with stale/attacker content; navigating into any child re-triggers the gate.

workflow: When a plan-checker warning is non-blocking but touches security-adjacent code, log it as a todo before advancing rather than silently deferring — keeps the gap visible without blocking execution.
Independently re-running acceptance/security tests after an executor's self-reported PASS (rather than trusting the summary) caught nothing wrong here but is worth doing on security-critical waves.

ScheduleWakeup delay calculations must be recomputed against the actual current time right before scheduling — reusing a delay computed earlier (before a quota-reset gap) produced a wake time ~25 minutes later than intended.
When a stray/duplicate scheduled wakeup can't be cleanly retracted, it's safe to let it fire as a no-op as long as the session state at fire-time is checked before taking any action.

friction: gsd-tools query commit reported `commit_failed` multiple times despite commits landing successfully — required manual `git log` verification each time (known false negative).
Generic gap-analysis parser broke on control characters in the `rendered` field, requiring a direct/manual invocation of the check.

REQUIREMENTS.md SDK-READ-01/02 checkboxes were incorrectly marked complete by Wave 1/2 executors before their full acceptance criteria (service deletions in Wave 6) were met, requiring two rounds of manual reversion.
zsh glob syntax failed when grepping for deletion-blocking importers across apps/web/src, requiring a redo with corrected syntax.
`git fetch` could not reach GitHub from the sandboxed session (no network), forcing reliance on the last-known local `origin/main` ref.
ScheduleWakeup was first called with a delay computed from a stale pre-quota-gap timestamp, producing an incorrect wake time (04:35 instead of the intended 04:10) that had to be corrected.

Plan 68.2-06 revealed a planner coverage gap only during execution: several web components consuming SealedChildRef/ResolvedChild data (FileBrowser.tsx, SelectionActionBar.tsx, ContextMenu.tsx, SharedFileBrowser.tsx) were not owned by any plan, discovered late enough to require ad hoc scope-mapping work rather than being caught at plan-check time.
